rows.headline: How taxation affects your Senior Citizen Savings Scheme returns
rows.hook: Taxation lowers actual SCSS take-home returns

modes.bear: For seniors in the 30% tax bracket, the effective return drops significantly, making other tax-efficient instruments potentially more attractive.
modes.bull: SCSS offers a high 8.2% sovereign-backed return, which remains competitive for many seniors even after accounting for income tax.
modes.simple: SCSS is a safe government scheme for seniors. However, the interest you earn is added to your income and taxed, so you do not keep the full 8.2%.

rows.summary: Interest earned from the Senior Citizen Savings Scheme (SCSS) is fully taxable according to the investor's income tax slab. While the current interest rate is 8.2%, the actual take-home amount depends on the individual's total annual income. Tax is deducted at source if the total interest earned exceeds ₹50,000 in a financial year. Indian retail investors must calculate post-tax yields to accurately compare SCSS with other fixed-income options.
rows.why_it_matters: Retirement planning requires calculating post-tax rather than gross returns.
rows.winners_losers: Government collects tax / High-income seniors lose yield
